newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market light $67 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market light $67 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold Monday in a limited test at $67.00 per cwt, unchanged from light sales on Friday, feedlot sources said.
About 2,500 steers and heifers that would likely grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 2,000 in Kansas, they said.
Further bids at $67.00 were passed by owners pricing cattle mostly at $68, with a few at $69.00.
Most feedlots remained extremely current in marketings this spring following several weeks of strong beef demand, they said.

The currentness was reflected in last Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, which showed April marketings at 102.0 percent of a year ago, above pre-report analyst estimates that averaged 101.0 percent.
Beef clearance during the weekend was said to be moderate, which could underpin fed cattle prices if retailers book some "fill-in" orders, market sources said.
Beef prices Monday were quoted up $0.06 to $1.17 per cwt, with 166 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavy choice beef was up $0.06 at $105.79.
